about.title: Hughson Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Hughson is a small Stanislaus County community, and many residents drive to nearby Modesto or Turlock for specialized care, or rely on local clinics for everyday medical needs. When something goes wrong during that care — a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, a medication mix-up — patients are often left with more questions than answers. California law sets specific rules for these cases, including a shortened filing window and a requirement that a qualified medical expert review the claim before it can move forward. We evaluate medical records to determine whether the standard of care was met under the MICRA framework. There's no cost to get that conversation started, and no obligation to move forward afterward.

items.title: We Understand the MICRA Clock
items.desc: California generally gives one year from discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. We can help you track these deadlines before they close.

items.title: Expert Review Comes First
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert is almost always required to support a malpractice claim, we typically arrange that review before deciding how to proceed.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, No Guesswork
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. That includes handling the required 90-day pre-suit notice on your behalf.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after treatment in Hughson — does that mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor result alone doesn't establish malpractice. We would need to review whether the care fell below the accepted medical standard, usually with input from a qualified medical expert.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a required 90-day pre-suit notice before a lawsuit can be filed, so earlier review is better.

items.question: Are damages limited in California malpractice cases?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to that same cap.
